problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc,$ $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨1,-2,-1⟩$, $c=⟨-4,5,-1⟩$, and  $u=⟨1,1,4⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$

feedback.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc,$ $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨-1,-1,4⟩$, $c=⟨-3,-8,14⟩$, and  $u=⟨5,-10,-14⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
feedback.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -8 \\ 14\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ -14\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s-3t=5 \\ -s-8t=-10 \\ 4s+14t=-14\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ -1 & -8 & -10 \\ 4 & 14 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -15 \\ 4 & 14 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -15 \\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s-3t=5 \\ t=3 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
t=3.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-s-3t & =5 \\ -s-3(3) & =5 \\ -s-9 & =5 \\ s & =-14.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=-14,\,t=3,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=-14b+3c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=(-14)\cdot 3=-42.$
